title: High-Difficulty Quantitative Sets
tagline: Year 4 — Multi-step problems on repeated replacement, partnerships, alternating work, races and combined interest

introduction.overview: High-difficulty questions are not more advanced mathematics; they are longer chains in which a small slip early on ruins the result. Typical forms are repeated replacement in a mixture, partnerships with changing capital, alternating work, relative motion with turn-arounds, and compound interest with changing rates. The method is to define variables clearly, build the chain step by step and verify with a rough estimate.
introduction.placementRelevance: These are the questions that separate top scores in company aptitude papers; attempt them after the easier ones.
introduction.realWorldContext: Project planning with phased resources and investments with changing capital have the same structure.

learningObjectives: Handle repeated replacement with a geometric factor
Split partnership profit by capital × time

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Replacement: milk left = initial × (1 − x/V)ⁿ. Partnership: profit ∝ capital × time. Work in phases: add the fractions completed.

coreDefinitions: Replacement: removing part of a mixture and refilling with another liquid.
Capital-time product: capital multiplied by months invested.
Phase: a stretch of time with a fixed set of workers or speeds.
Turn-around: reversing direction during a journey.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A long problem is a short problem repeated or stitched together. Find the repeating unit.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Define the unknown, write the first phase, then the second, and so on; add or multiply as the structure demands.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Replacement
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: n replacements of x from volume V.

mainNarrative: A vessel with 100 L of milk has 10 L removed and replaced by water three times. Milk left = 100 × 0.9³ = 72.9 L.
Three partners invest ₹6,000, ₹8,000 and ₹10,000 for 12, 9 and 6 months. Capital × time: 72,000 : 72,000 : 60,000 = 6 : 6 : 5.
A tank is filled by pipe A in 6 hours; after 2 hours pipe B (12 hours alone) joins. In 2 hours A fills 1/3. Together they fill 1/4 per hour, so the remaining 2/3 takes 8/3 h; total 4⅔ h.
A sum at 10% in year 1 and 20% in year 2 grows by a factor of 1.1 × 1.2 = 1.32, a total of 32%.
Check each result against a rough estimate (for example the tank must take more than 2 hours and less than 6).

deepDiveAspects.title: Alternate work
deepDiveAspects.content: Compute the work per cycle, count full cycles, then handle the leftover units.

deepDiveAspects.title: Rate changes
deepDiveAspects.content: When the rate changes in the middle, split the time and compute each part separately.

solvedExamples.title: Replacement
solvedExamples.question: 100 L of milk: 10 L removed and replaced by water, three times. How much milk is left?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Each step removes 10% of the current milk.

solvedExamples.title: Partnership
solvedExamples.question: Investments ₹6,000, ₹8,000, ₹10,000 for 12, 9, 6 months. Find the ratio of profit shares.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Time matters as much as capital.

solvedExamples.title: Phased work
solvedExamples.question: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 h. After 2 h, pipe B (12 h alone) opens too. Total time?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Find the repeating unit (a factor) or split into phases and add the results.

placementTips.recruiterInsight: Neat intermediate numbers show you are on the right track.
